newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile cobalt court cases drag on.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile cobalt court cases drag on.

text.p: The two separate court cases which led to the suspension of U.S. Stockpile cobalt sales look set to drag on with no clear timetable for a final outcome, a lawyer for the government agency said.
"We don't have any kind of feel for a timetable," U.S. Stockpile counsel Essie Schloss said.
Lawyers for Minor Metals or officials at the company were not immediately available for comment.
Stockpile has said all cobalt sales will remain suspended until its legal entanglements with Minor Metals have been resolved.
Friday, Stockpile and Minor Metals Inc both filed additional information to the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, Schloss said. There was no oral hearing.
Trader Minor Metals complained to the Claims court that Stockpile erred on two counts in handling its sealed bid sale of cobalt in March.

The judge dismissed the first complaint but ruled that the second issue of price matching or so called domestic preference provision in a sealed bid, although within the authority of the Stockpile to enforce, was procedurally improper.
Both parties were asked to confer on this issue and report back June 13. A preliminary injunction was granted to Minor Metals in May to stop the March sale continuing.

In a separate case in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, Minor Metals asked the judge to reconsider his ruling which dismissed complaints by the trading company against Stockpile regarding the February negotiated cobalt sale.
Schloss said the Virginia court judge has asked Stockpile for more information, due by June 18, in order to carry out his ruling review.
